rationale: Positives: The agent verified the user via email, asked for confirmation before making changes, and successfully updated both orders’ shipping addresses and the user’s default address to 592 Elm Avenue as requested. Negatives (policy-breaking): 1) The agent asserted product/availability/price details for the “cheapest tablet” (7-inch, 128GB, $941.03) without clear support from the product tool output, and did not confirm availability; the visible variants did not include that option, and the only clearly available variant shown was different and more expensive. 2) The agent did not confirm that a tablet exists in order #W1603792 or read the item_id from that order before performing the exchange; instead, it used item IDs not supported by prior reads. 3) The agent stated a precise refund amount ($77.65) without any tool output supporting that calculation. 4) It also stated that both orders were pending without reading status for #W1603792. These constitute inventing unsupported facts and performing writes without sufficient read verification, which fails the policy’s requirements to avoid fabrication and to inspect with read-only tools before committing changes.
